scenario.description: A small software engineering team is tasked with implementing a new API endpoint for user profile updates. The objective is to design, develop, and test this endpoint while adhering to specific performance and security constraints. The team consists of a Lead Developer, a Backend Engineer, and a QA Engineer. The Lead Developer is responsible for overall design and coordination. The Backend Engineer implements the API logic and database interactions. The QA Engineer writes and executes test cases. A crucial performance constraint is that the API response time for the new endpoint must not exceed 250.75 milliseconds. Additionally, all data exchanges through this endpoint must be encrypted using TLS 1.3 or higher. The fully connected topology ensures every agent can directly communicate with any other agent, facilitating immediate feedback and discussions on critical constraints. This medium-structural-complexity task evaluates how effectively these precise numerical and security constraints are propagated and maintained through 18 turns of iterative discussion, design, and validation in a tightly integrated team environment.
